ReleaseTrain.io — Software Ecosystem Framework

A practical reference for the platform architecture, data flow, and API surface area. ReleaseTrain ingests ecosystem signals (GitHub, CVE/NVD, Reddit), enriches and classifies updates, and exposes the results via a backend API and triage UI.

🌐 Live: releasetrain.io 💻 Client: SE4CPS/releasetrain-client 📋 Board: SE4CPS Project 24
2xx/3xx OK 4xx Client 5xx Server

Checks use GET and only report status codes (2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx).

Introduction

ReleaseTrain is built to help teams keep a steady pace with software ecosystem updates. It collects update signals, improves their quality, classifies impact (type, security, breaking changes), and presents actionable results for triage.

How to use this document

  • Start with Architecture to understand the end to end flow.
  • Use the API section as a direct reference for queries and examples.
  • Use Test & Discovery to validate routes and detect duplicates.

Practical note: the structure below is intentionally simple and traditional: a fixed table of contents on the left, and the reference content on the right, with stable anchor links.

Agentic AI vs Traditional Software

Capability Description / Example Tech What’s Different
Data Access & Reasoning Pulls GitHub, CVE/NVD, and Reddit; decides urgency: 
if (cve.severity >= 7) trigger_triage(); else ignore();

const prompt = `
I have a new CVE and a list of affected repos.
Consider GitHub data and Reddit sentiment.
Should we triage urgently? Explain.`;
const result = llm.invoke(prompt);
 Python, LangChain, pymongo Beyond fixed rules: uses context + language models for decisions.
Action Orchestration Sequences multi tool workflows; updates backend, notifies UI. LangChain Agents, FastAPI/Python Dynamic tool use vs static pipelines.
Contextual Interpretation LLM/RAG cross correlates signals and sentiment. Azure OpenAI (gpt-4o), LlamaIndex Understands text + relationships across sources.

Runtime & Platform

Layer Platform Notes
Bots (GitHub, CVE, Reddit) Ubuntu 22.04 LTS Python, APIs / feeds
Data Lake MongoDB Atlas Schemaless raw + enriched; indexes on versionId, etc.
Backend Node.js + Express NGINX reverse proxy; JSON APIs; CORS enabled
ML / Classification Ubuntu 22.04 LTS Daily classifiers: Type/Security/Breaking; Sentiment (planned)
LLM / RAG Azure gpt-4o, augmentation over Reddit/CVE/Release Notes
Frontend Web Graph/UML/Updates/Triage modules (MIT)

API

The API reference is grouped by domain (Reddit, Versions, Components, Aggregations) so it reads like a handbook.

Conventions

  • Base URL: https://releasetrain.io (examples below are clickable).
  • Date format: YYYYMMDD unless noted.
  • Range helper: many endpoints implicitly limit to “last 2 years through tomorrow”.
  • Headers (cursor paging): X-Next-Cursor, X-Total-Count, Link, X-Page, X-Limit.
  • Status checks: every GET row below has a Check button that runs a GET request and shows the HTTP status.

Quick API Checks (All GET)

Use this to sanity-check routing and availability. Green = 2xx/3xx. Yellow = 4xx. Red = 5xx/network.

Endpoint Action
/api/health
/api/meta
/api/reddit?limit=25
/api/v/?q=chrome,firefox

Reddit

Method Endpoint Description Example Sample
POST /api/reddit Upsert a post by redditId. Adds updatedAt. 
curl -X POST "https://releasetrain.io/api/reddit" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"redditId":"1nq0h33","title":"Example","created_utc":"2025-09-28T12:00:00Z"}'
 
{"success":true,"message":"Reddit post added/updated.","redditId":"1nq0h33"}
GET /api/reddit Newest first listing with page/limit or stable cursor pagination.
/api/reddit?limit=25 
{ "data":[ { "title":"...", "created_utc":"..." }, ... ] }
GET /api/reddit?month=YYYYMM Monthly window filter when created_utc is ISO (YYYY-MM-...).
/api/reddit?month=202507&limit=25 
{ "data":[ ... ] }
GET /api/reddit?isUpdateRelated=true Filter by existence and (optionally) value of metadata.isUpdateRelated.
/api/reddit?isUpdateRelated=true&limit=25 
{ "data":[ ... ] }
GET /api/reddit?isUpdateRelated=true&isUpdateRelatedValue=false Only docs where metadata.isUpdateRelated exists and is false.
/api/reddit?isUpdateRelated=true&isUpdateRelatedValue=false&limit=25 
{ "data":[ ... ] }
GET /api/reddit?isUpdateRelated=false Only docs where metadata.isUpdateRelated does not exist.
/api/reddit?isUpdateRelated=false&limit=25 
{ "data":[ ... ] }
GET /api/reddit/count Total posts in the last 2 years (inclusive to “tomorrow”).
/api/reddit/count 
{"totalRedditPosts":248}
GET /api/reddit/stats/summary Summary totals for a date range on created_utc (string compare).
/api/reddit/stats/summary?start=20240101&end=20241231 
{ "success":true, "totals":{ "total":..., "risky":... } }
GET /api/reddit/stats/by-month Monthly counts for labeled training distribution.
/api/reddit/stats/by-month?startMonth=202401&endMonth=202412 
{ "success":true, "data":[{"month":"2024-01","count":...}, ...] }
GET /api/reddit/by-subreddit Filter by exact subreddit(s), case-insensitive; optional minScore, minComments, fields, page, limit.
/api/reddit/by-subreddit?q=programming
/api/reddit/by-subreddit?...&minScore=50... 
{ "page":2, "limit":25, "count":25, "subreddits":["programming","technology"], "data":[ ... ] }
GET /api/reddit/query/positive All docs where metadata.predicted.positiveScore > 0.5.
/api/reddit/query/positive 
{ "total":N, "minScore":0.5, "data":[ ... ] }
GET /api/reddit/query/cve Search for CVE patterns across title, author_description, first comment, and comments. Default q is CVE-.
/api/reddit/query/cve?q=CVE-&limit=25 
{ "q":"CVE-", "commentsOnly":false, "data":[ ... ] }
GET /api/reddit/query/cve?commentsOnly=true Search only in comments.body.
/api/reddit/query/cve?q=CVE-&commentsOnly=true&limit=25 
{ "commentsOnly":true, "data":[ ... ] }
GET /api/reddit/:redditId Fetch one by redditId or Mongo _id.
/api/reddit/1nq0h33 
{ "_id":"...", "redditId":"1nq0h33", ... }

Method Endpoint Description Example Sample

/api/v/latest10?q=chrome&limit=10

GET /api/v/search?channel=patch Filter by release channel (major|minor|patch|cve).

GET /api/v/search?isCve=true Filter CVE items explicitly.

{ "data":[ ... ] }
GET /api/v/search?start=YYYYMMDD&end=YYYYMMDD Date range on versionReleaseDate.
/api/v/search?q=chrome&start=20250101&end=20251231... 
{ "data":[ ... ] }
GET /api/v/search?fields=versionId,versionNumber Projection allow-list using fields.
/api/v/search?q=chrome&fields=versionId,versionNumber,versionReleaseDate... 
{ "data":[ { "versionId":"...", "versionNumber":"...", "versionReleaseDate":"..." }, ... ] }
GET /api/v/stats/by-month Counts by month and channel (major/minor/patch/cve).
/api/v/stats/by-month?startMonth=202401&endMonth=202412&q=chrome,firefox 
{ "success":true, "totalRows":N, "data":[{"month":"2024-01","channel":"patch","count":...}, ...] }
GET /api/dashboard/mltl-risk Dashboard: versions with MLTL risk (no date range limit). Optional q filter.
/api/dashboard/mltl-risk?q=chrome,firefox 
{ "success":true, "totalVersions":N, "aggregate":{...}, "components":[ ... ] }
GET /api/v/count Total versions in last 2 years.
/api/v/count 
{"totalVersions":1221}
GET /api/v/ Latest versions (last 2 years). Optional q=comma-separated components; mobile limit smaller.
/api/v/?q=chrome,firefox 
{ "versions":[ { "versionProductName":"chrome", ... }, ... ] }
GET /api/v/fc Forecast next release for a component via releasetrain-forecast.
/api/v/fc?q=chrome 
[ { "component":"chrome", "releaseDate":"..." } ]
GET /api/v/fcc Forecast coinciding release dates for a set of components.
/api/v/fcc?q=chrome,firefox 
[ { "component":"...", "coincideReleaseDate":"..." } ]
GET /api/v/:id Fetch by Mongo _id.
/api/v/660c38fce3cba9423e4f8f23 
{ "versionProductName":"...", ... }
GET /api/v/versionId/:versionId Fetch by stable versionId.
/api/v/versionId/20250217component1.2.3 
{ "versionNumber":"1.2.3", ... }
POST /api/v Insert a version; cleans/normalizes versionNumber, sets timestamps/search tags. 
curl -X POST "https://releasetrain.io/api/v" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{ "versionId":"20250901foo1.2.3", "versionProductName":"foo", "versionNumber":"1.2.3", "versionReleaseDate":"20250901" }'
 
{ "_id":"...", "versionId":"20250901foo1.2.3", ... }
GET /api/v/aggregate/byDate Count of versions released on a given day.
/api/v/aggregate/byDate?date=20250723 
{ "success":true, "date":"20250723", "count": 42 }

Security

All endpoints are JSON over HTTPS behind NGINX. MongoDB Atlas connections use authenticated URIs with TLS. CORS is enabled for API consumption; custom headers are exposed for cursor pagination. Certificates are provisioned via Let’s Encrypt/Certbot. API key based access is supported (rotate regularly).

Current Limitations

  • API keys not yet rotated on a schedule.
  • Inconsistent component labels in some frontend views.
  • No automated security tests (authn/z, header policy, schema validation) yet.
  • Upstream inputs (Reddit/CVE feeds) require stricter validation.

Next Steps (Hardening)

  • Move secrets to environment variables / vault; enforce rotation and per service keys.
  • Add request schema validation (e.g., zod/ajv) and output allow lists.
  • Enable basic WAF rules, rate limiting, and IP allow lists for write endpoints.
  • Automate CI security tests (SAST/DAST), dependency checks, and SBOM.
  • Structured audit logs (success/failure, auth context, redaction for PII).
